title: Recorders: Selenium IDE, BugBug and Ghost Inspector — and why code wins

videos.script: Recorders promise a test without code. You click through the shop, and the tool writes down what you did. {{record}} This lesson looks at three of them. Selenium IDE saves your clicks in a file of JSON. BugBug and Ghost Inspector keep them in a service, and run them on a schedule. {{side}} None of them can be operated here, because this machine has no screen. So you read what a recording is made of, one step at a time. {{codegen}} Playwright has a recorder too, called codegen. You ask the part of it that names elements what it would pick on the shop. Most answers are good. One of them is the price that happens to be on screen. {{run}} Then you run two recordings as tests. The first fails on the random id from lesson two. The second fails because nothing empties the basket. {{rewrite}} The same check, written by hand with the page object from lesson twelve, passes. {{change}} Last, the shop's button gets new words. You count the lines each version has to change. Four in the recording, one in the page object. {{verdict}} A recorder is a fine way to start a test. Code is where a test can live.
